Shared Coastlines: Joint Climate Adaptation in the Kattegat Region

Shared Coastlines brings together six municipalities in Denmark and Sweden to plan coastal protection across municipal and national borders. Rising sea levels and more frequent storm surges threaten homes, roads and harbours along the Kattegat, and solutions in one municipality can move the problem to its neighbour.

The project will develop a joint risk map, test three types of coastal protection at pilot sites in Grenaa, Ebeltoft and Falkenberg, and produce a shared planning guide that can be used by other coastal municipalities in the programme area.
Aarhus University, Department of Civil Engineering, Denmark

Work package 1 covers project management and communication. Work package 2 develops the joint risk map, based on data from the Danish Climate Atlas (Klimaatlas) and its Swedish equivalent. Work package 3 covers the pilot sites, and work package 4 the planning guide.

The pilot in Grenaa tests a combination of beach nourishment and dunes. The pilot in Ebeltoft tests a raised promenade that doubles as a flood barrier, and the pilot in Falkenberg tests managed realignment of a low-lying meadow.

By the end of the project, the partners will have a common method for assessing coastal risk, tested solutions at three sites, and a guide that has been discussed with at least 20 other municipalities. The results will be presented at a final conference in Halmstad in 2029.

Kommunalbestyrelsen besluttede den 30. oktober 2026 at godkende, at kommunen søger om midler fra Interreg-programmet som ledende partner i projektet Shared Coastlines, og at kommunens egenfinansiering på 496.000 euro afholdes inden for rammen til klimatilpasning i budget 2027–2029.
Beslutningen blev truffet med 23 stemmer for og 4 imod. Mindretallet ønskede, at projektet først blev drøftet i Teknik- og Miljøudvalget.
